title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-008: Is RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_UPDATE domain separator used in Fiat-Shamir hash?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_UPDATE domain separator is defined in the EIP-7594 specification and implemented within ckzg4844 C library. Prysm's kzg.go wraps ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which internally uses this domain separator. Prysm does not implement the Fiat-Shamir hash directly - it is entirely within ckzg4844.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Domain separator usage delegated to ckzg4844 reference implementation. No bypass at Prysm layer.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Fiat-Shamir challenge entirely within ckzg4844. Prysm passes inputs without modifying challenge computation.

title: Supporting Check: Does the Fiat-Shamir challenge r correctly bind ALL input commitments, cell_indices, cells, and proofs?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Per EIP-7594 spec, the Fiat-Shamir challenge r is computed as: r = hash(RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_UPDATE || len(commitments) || commitments || cell_indices || cells). title: Supporting Check: Is the random challenge r resistant to attacker influence?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Attacker influence on r: r = hash(domain || inputs). Attacker controls inputs (commitment bytes, cell data). If attacker can choose inputs to produce a desired r value, they could potentially break the binding. However, this requires inverting SHA-256 (preimage resistance), which is computationally infeasible. Standard Fiat-Shamir security argument applies.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: r is SHA-256 hash of inputs. Attacker cannot predict r without knowing inputs first (random oracle model).

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: r is computationally unpredictable under SHA-256 preimage resistance.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Challenge unpredictability invariant holds under SHA-256 security assumption.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Challenge r is SHA-256 based. Attacker influence computationally infeasible.

title: Supporting Check: Can an attacker exploit weak entropy to forge proofs?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Fiat-Shamir transforms do not use runtime entropy. The challenge r is deterministically computed from the inputs themselves (commitment data, cell data). No external random number generator is used. Weak entropy attacks do not apply to Fiat-Shamir - the security comes from the hash function's collision resistance, not from an external randomness source.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No entropy source used. Challenge is deterministic. Weak entropy attack does not apply.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Fiat-Shamir is deterministic; no entropy weakness possible.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: No entropy-based attack surface. Deterministic challenge.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Fiat-Shamir is deterministic. Weak entropy attack concept does not apply.
